item.description:
Portside gets better at staying where you work: tabs you can arrange and move
between panes, folders that remember how you sorted them, a Go to Folder field
that completes paths, drops that land on the folder you point at, and panes
that follow a folder you rename.

### What's new

- Tabs can be dragged to reorder, jumped to with ⌘1–⌘9, and moved whole to
  the other pane by drag or ⇧⌘M. A moved tab keeps its folder, selection,
  sort, and embedded terminal session.
- A folder you re-sort remembers that sort: arriving there again — in any tab
  of either pane, and after a relaunch — applies it. Folders you never
  re-sorted keep the tab's sort. The most recent 500 folders are remembered.
- Go to Folder (⌘⇧G) completes folder names as you type (Tab accepts the
  completion) and offers a menu of recently typed paths — the last 50 that
  resolved to a real folder.
- Settings adds a pane text size (Small, Medium, Large), a choice of terminal
  shell (leave it empty for your login shell), and a terminal text size
  (9–24 pt) that applies live to open sessions.
- Dropping onto a folder row drops into that folder — the `..` row included —
  and a drag that rests over a folder springs it open. Packages, symbolic
  links, and a dragged row itself never act as drop targets.
- When the folder a pane shows is renamed or moved on the same disk, the pane
  follows it — selection, cursor, and per-folder memories intact — instead of
  reporting it gone.

### Known limitations

- A followed rename ends what it cannot carry: a confirmation dialog or a
  running transfer rooted in the renamed folder is cancelled with a notice,
  and a folder moved to another volume is not followed. Only local folders
  follow; SFTP cannot prove folder identity.
- Path completion and the recents menu are local-only and live in the Go to
  Folder dialog, not in the header's inline path editor.
- A pane's only tab cannot move to the other pane, and a tab with an open
  dialog or a transfer in progress can neither move nor close.
- There is no gesture yet to make a folder forget its remembered sort.
- A changed terminal shell applies to shells opened afterwards; open sessions
  keep theirs. Terminal font family and theme are not configurable yet.
